thread:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV2 — cluster tp-mg01 reporting repeated collective bootstrap failures for tensor-parallel jobs. Multiple containers restarted in the last 3m. Auto-escalation to on-call.
cheng liu: Acked. I'm oncall, joining now. Which jobs are affected?
maya rao: Job ids: [job-9876, job-9879]. Both are TP=2, PP=1. Logs show repeated NCCL bootstrap timeouts then a CUDA launch failure.
samir khan: Seeing the same in node logs: 'NCCL WARN bootstrap timeout waiting for peers' followed by 'CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED (error 702)'. Also OOM spike right before restart on gpu0.
riley park: @cheng do we have customer-impact yet? Any external-facing services?
cheng liu: Quick check: two API frontends routed to model-hosting cluster. Customer telemetry shows 5xx surge for model inference calls starting ~2480012200.
ashley jensen: Customer Alert: Account acme-inc reported failures on >50% requests. Support already opened a ticket.
incident-bot: Pager duty acknowledged by cheng liu. Escalation level: SEV2. Handoff to oncall in 15m if not resolved.
maya rao: Pasting relevant snippet from pod logs:
```
[2026-07-12T10:12:33Z] NCCL WARN Bootstrap timeout: attempted 5 of 5
[2026-07-12T10:12:33Z] NCCL ERROR unhandled communicator error
[2026-07-12T10:12:34Z] cuda runtime error: unspecified launch failure (702)
[2026-07-12T10:12:34Z] Container restart (OOM?)
```
samir khan: Also attaching node-level nvidia-smi at 10:11: shows one process at 100% mem on gpu0 and persistently high utilization on gpu1. Possible memory leak in recent rollout.
riley park: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Drain the affected node to stop new TP jobs. 2) Force-restart container runtime on that node. 3) Re-route critical traffic to fallback single-GPU model variant.
cheng liu: Let's do 1 and 3 in parallel. Schedule drain on node mg-node-17 now, and switch routing for the acme-inc served model to fallback model-v1-slim.
maya rao: Commands I'm running:
```
kubectl cordon mg-node-17
kubectl drain mg-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```
samir khan: Also bumping NCCL debug env to INFO and enabling async error handling on the pod template to collect more details. Patch:
```
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1
```
ashley jensen: Routing change applied for acme-inc -> model-v1-slim. Confirmed on load-balancer side. Traffic at 50% routed away for now.
riley park: Any chance this is related to the kernel that went out in last deploy? We rolled a runtime image last night (runtime:v3.4.1).
maya rao: Correlating: both failed jobs were scheduled after the runtime:v3.4.1 rollout. I'm reverting a small subset of hosts to runtime:v3.4.0 for comparison.
incident-bot: Note: next oncall pager is riley park at 2480013345.
samir khan: Temporary workaround: scaling down parallel degree on queued TP jobs prevents immediate reoccurrence. I've queued a rollout that forces TP=1 for non-critical experiments.
cheng liu: After drain, mg-node-17 shows no new TP pods. Restarted docker runtime on that node as well. Monitoring for stabilisation.
maya rao: Logs after restart show initial bootstraps succeeding but one other node returned a transient NCCL allreduce error. I'm keeping NCCL_DEBUG logs collected and pushing to /tmp/collective-debug-248001.
samir khan: Found a repeatable stack trace referencing a communicator ID mismatch during bootstrap handshake. Suspect race during communicator creation with the new runtime change.
ashley jensen: Support confirmed acme-inc errors dropped from 55% -> 2% after routing change. Notified customer success and ACME POC.
riley park: Good. Next steps: 1) Rollback runtime:v3.4.1 from a subset of hosts. 2) Keep nodes drained until we validate. 3) Run a small-scale soak test with TP=2 on canary hosts.
cheng liu: Assigning follow-up to eng-runtime: @maya and @samir to own rollback validation. I'll stay on until the canary passes, then update SEV ticket.
maya rao: Pushing a temporary ingress rule to prefer hosts in region-us-east-2 for critical traffic to avoid cross-rack NVLink paths while we investigate.
samir khan: If we see recurrence, plan B is to force software fallback to NCCL P2P disable for suspect hosts and fall back to PCIe (will degrade perf but prevent hangs).
incident-bot: SEV2 ongoing. Active responders: cheng liu, maya rao, samir khan, riley park, ashley jensen. Update cadence: 10m.
cheng liu: I'll hand off to @riley in 12m if stable. Leaving notes in the ticket: suspected communicator race introduced by runtime:v3.4.1 leading to NCCL bootstrap failure and CUDA launch errors; customer impact - degraded inference for acme-inc mitigated via routing.
riley park: Acknowledged. I'll take over if any flareups. :eyes:
ashley jensen: Filing postmortem stub and customer incident communication draft now.
cheng liu: Thanks team — monitoring for next 30m then close if no regressions. :thumbsup:
